summary: 48-ft steel tower on Telegraph Hill, first operated 1939, staffed to 1942; FFLOS lists it as a former lookout and does not say whether a tower stands, but The Pinehills says residents climb a tower there today.

facts.status_note: FFLOS lists the site as a former lookout and does not say whether a tower stands. The Pinehills' community history says a 48-ft tower was built there in 1939 and that residents climb it today. The history page is not a site survey.

visit.trail_note: Only The Pinehills' history page describes a tower on the hill today, and it says residents climb it. Ask The Pinehills before visiting.

events.note: NHLR: a replacement 48-ft tower moved to Telegraph Hill. FFLOS: first operated 1939. The Pinehills: a 48-ft tower built there for fire detection that year.
Staffed until 1942 per FFLOS; served until 1942 per NHLR.
Registered on the Former Fire Lookout Sites register on September 3, 2008.

evidence.supports: 48-ft steel tower first operated in 1939 and staffed until 1942
evidence.quote: This 48' steel tower was first operated in 1939 and was staffed until 1942.

evidence.supports: a replacement 48-ft tower relocated to Telegraph Hill in 1939 and served until 1942
evidence.quote: In 1939, a replacement 48’ tower was relocated on Telegraph Hill and served until 1942.

evidence.supports: The Pinehills says a 48-ft tower was built on Telegraph Hill in 1939 for fire detection
evidence.quote: In 1939 a 48’ tower was built for fire detection.

evidence.supports: The Pinehills says residents climb the tower today
evidence.quote: Residents climb it nowadays for spectacular views all the way to Plymouth Beach and Provincetown in the distance.

evidence.quote: One of the highest points in The Pinehills once served as the ideal place for Native Americans to send and receive smoke signals.

notes_for_editor: Status is contested, so the brief's 'gone' should not be published as settled. FFLOS calls it a former site and does not say whether a tower stands; The Pinehills community history says a 48-ft tower was built there in 1939 and that residents climb it today. The Pinehills page is marketing-style history, not a survey, and no other source read confirms or denies a standing tower. Access is unknown and the story says so; do not encourage climbing. The NHLR, FFLOS and Pinehills pages agree on 1939 and 1942; they differ on wording (moved in, first operated, built). The story no longer says the sources disagree on standing, because FFLOS does not address it. Do not confuse this with the Telegraph Hill in Hull, Massachusetts, or the Telegraph Hill in Lawrence County, Ohio, which the search results also returned. Brief record (gone, 250 ft / 76 m, coordinates, 2008 registration) matches FFLOS; no corrections proposed beyond the status question.
